check: measurement hygiene: an inflated error count that was my own doing
whatHappened: A health check reported 3 ERROR/Exception lines in the profile log. The file actually contains zero [ERROR] lines and one benign spawner message from 09:12.
cause: The count came from piping Get-Content into Select-String. When Set-Location had already failed on a relative path in the same session, the shell's own NativeCommandError and RemoteException text entered the pipeline and was counted as if it were log content.
correctMethod: Two independent readings agree. Reading the file with a shared FileStream, which is required anyway because the live process holds the log open, gives 0 [ERROR] and 1 spawner line. Select-String pointed directly at the file path gives the same.
whyItMatters: An inflated error count in a 24h stability run is exactly the kind of finding that would be reported as a real defect. Counting your own tool's noise as evidence is a false positive with real consequences, and this is the seventh such artifact this session.
sessionFalseAlarmTally: ChunkGateState flagged as a test class - case-insensitive match on teSt inside GateState
PaletteResolverTest flagged as assertion-free - the pattern missed a private assert helper
110 blocking calls - Optional.get counted as blocking
Chinese comments read as mojibake - console code page, not the file
two jars with identical SHA - a failed Get-FileHash left the previous variable in place
certificate cited a missing line - the log is UTF-16LE and the search was UTF-8
3 ERROR lines - the shell's own error text entered the pipeline
pattern: Six of the seven were a check that could not distinguish the target from its surroundings. Recording the tally because the rate is itself informative: roughly one in ten of my checks needed correcting, and in every case the correction came from reading the underlying bytes rather than re-running the same query.
